## Research and decisions (agent, M5)

These settle the points the umbrella left open, so the sub-issues can be filed. I checked each one against the repo as it is today (`crates/post/src/machine`, `crates/cl/src/cl/moves.rs`, the `.cps` engine and the stock sims). Each decision gives its reason and what was dropped.

**D1: build order.** Wire EDM first, as a thin end-to-end slice: schema → condition table → 2-axis contour → wire post → wire verify → UI. Then taper and 4-axis, skims, tabs and burnout. Sinker EDM comes last.
*Why:* a 2-axis wire contour reuses what exists: geo2d offsetting, the 2D contour ride, lead-in/out and the `.cps` engine. Sinker needs electrode generation from 3D faces, the largest new piece. A thin slice proves the machine kind, CL, post and verify seams before anything is built on them.
*Dropped:* building the schema for both kinds first. Sinker's keys would be guessed before any sinker op exists to test them.

**D2: wire geometry in the CL uses the existing tool pose, not a new field.** A wire move's `to` is its point on the lower programmed plane, and `Move.pose` (already a unit vector tip → shank, used for multi-axis since M5.1) is the wire's direction toward the upper guide. The upper point is derived at post time from the stated upper-plane height. Between endpoints both ends interpolate linearly, which is the ruled surface. A vertical 2-axis cut states no pose, so it posts as plain XY.
*Why:* the multi-axis pose already flows through dump, CL text, verify and post. Taper, variable taper and 4-axis then reduce to "a pose per move". Sync points become paired moves, and the crossing/fold check reads consecutive poses.
*Dropped:* a separate UV channel in `Move`. Every consumer (sim, verify, every post, the CL golden format) would need a second path, and a vertical cut would carry a meaningless zero UV.

**D3: sinker orbit is generated as explicit moves by default.** The motion crate expands circular/vector/planetary orbits into CL moves, so the stock sim verifies exactly what posts. A dialect that states a canned orbit word *may* later post the pattern compactly, but only after the expanded path has verified clean. That is a separate, later sub-issue, not part of the first slice.
*Why:* Prime Directive. A canned cycle is motion the sim never saw.

**D4: the condition table is per-machine user data in the `.mch` file**, under `edm.conditions[]`: `{ id, name, gap_mm (spark gap per side), wire_diameter_mm (wire) or undersize_mm (sinker), pass role (rough/skim/finish), notes }`. No vendor values are shipped. The library machine files carry an empty table, so an EDM op refuses by name ("machine states no condition for …") until the user fills it from their manual. Test fixtures use our own synthetic tables, marked as such.
*Why:* absent is not zero (`assets/machines/AGENTS.md`), and generator data is vendor material we must not copy.

**D5: dialects are data, starting from one generic ISO-style post per kind.** `wire-iso.cps` and `sinker-iso.cps` post the RS-274 motion words themselves (G0/G1/G2/G3, G90/G91). Every EDM-specific code comes from `.mch` `edm.codes`: taper on/off and how the angle or UV is written, AWT thread/cut, wire-tip disposal, condition select, compensation on/off and side. A missing code refuses the post by name. No vendor dialect is shipped. Supporting a real control means filling `edm.codes` from its manual, the same law as the M-codes held as data today.
*Why:* the umbrella's research shows G41/G42 and G21/G22 mean different things across wire controls, so no default table can be safe.

**D6: the research gaps.**
- **Tabs/bridges:** off by default. When on, count and width are required parameters with no invented default (no manufacturer-validated value exists). Slug analysis refuses an unsupported slug unless a tab or capture is set.
- **AWT and slug retention:** an `edm.awt` flag plus the codes as data. No universal procedure is assumed.
- **Orbit names:** CamCraft models the *geometry* (circular, vector, planetary). The machine states which it supports and the word for each. A pattern the machine does not list is refused.

**D7: verification.**
- **Wire:** 2.5D. The kerf region swept on the lower and upper planes (with the ruled surface between them for a taper) is checked against the part section at both planes for gouge, the start-hole and threading clearance through the full height, and the taper angle against the machine maximum and UV travel. Slug analysis uses geo2d region connectivity: which region becomes free when the cut closes.
- **Sinker:** reuses the existing 3-axis stock sim, with the electrode as the tool solid, plus a depth-datum check and orbit clearance.
- Both block the post on any flag, as today.

**D8: breakdown changes.** "Punch vs die" and "corner strategy / minimum radius" are a parameter and a refusal of the 2-axis contour op, so they fold into it. That leaves 19 sub-issues. A later "dialect canned orbit" item is noted under D3 and not filed now.

**D9: labels.** No `area:edm` label exists. Sub-issues use `enhancement`, `P2` (no user is blocked) and the closest `area:*`. Suggested to the owner: add an `area:edm` label.

**D10: what each sub-issue can prove without an EDM machine.** Goldens are posted against the synthetic fixture dialect and conditions, and the sims run on synthetic parts. Every PR in this family must state "not exercised on a real EDM control". A user with a real machine is asked to dry-run before any cut.

Next: filing the sub-issues, each with `Part of #290`, its dependencies and a "Done means" line.
